scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

estimate substitution when no accepted read

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-REQUESTER-FRAME.statement: Dispute surge is caused by incorrect bills that an AI agent can answer and fix.

H-AMI-READ-GAP.statement: Missing or delayed AMI reads from the MDMS lead to estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Problems in the contracted manual meter‑read process (missed reads, route issues) cause estimation errors and wrong bills.

H-RULE-CHANGE-BILLING.statement: A change to billing import validation rules introduced in August caused systematic mis‑billing.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The tariff change log contains no records, indicating no tariff changes were logged in the observed period.

Field route completion for Aug‑Sep is 0.88, below the target of 0.95, indicating the contracted manual meter‑read process is under‑performing and may be contributing to estimation errors and incorrect bills.
The observation shows more disputed bills with actual reads (1785) than estimated reads (1240), indicating the dispute surge is not solely driven by estimation gaps.
The dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 per month in June‑July to ~1,200 per month in August‑September, confirming a sustained surge.
Dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs SLA 3 days), indicating the surge is not causing response delays beyond the agreed limit.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports no tariff changes this year, indicating that tariff modifications are not a source of the dispute surge.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field stakeholder reports a shortage of three meter readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The contract clause shows that the utility may request route priority changes, but such changes require confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, establishing an approval control for route modifications.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The billing system estimated 320 accounts across 40 routes in the most recent cycle, showing a substantial volume of estimation that could influence bill accuracy.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The lagging routes tool shows 14 routes with low completion (sample completion 0.7), indicating many routes are underperforming and could contribute to estimation errors and disputes.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder confirms that MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned, indicating the utility can retrieve AMI reads. This reduces the plausibility that missing/delayed AMI reads are driving the dispute surge.
Among disputed estimated reads, 1184 AMI reads were taken before cutoff but rejected for high consumption yet still exported, while 56 lacked any read and were not exported.
